prompt.context_jp: 「行内で見つかったというのに 誰___置いてったかも分からないのか！？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 誰___置いてったかも分からないのか！？
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after the WH-word 誰.

feedback.correct_en: With interrogatives like 誰 asking for an unknown subject, が is required. The identity is new information being sought.
feedback.incorrect_en: 誰は is ungrammatical in this context — は cannot topicalize an unknown WH-subject. を would make 誰 the object, which doesn't fit 置く here.

contrast_examples.en: Who did it? (WH-subject — が)
He did nothing (known topic — は).

prompt.context_jp: 「見つかっただけで___… 何の解決にもなってない！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 見つかっただけで___…何の解決にもなってない！
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that signals 'merely X — but not more.'

feedback.correct_en: だけでは sets up a contrastive limitation: 'just finding it (and nothing more) solves nothing.' The は after で adds this contrastive 'only this much' nuance.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけでが is ungrammatical. だけでも would mean 'even just by finding it,' flipping the meaning positively.

contrast_examples.jp: 見るだけでは分からない。
contrast_examples.en: You can't understand just by looking (contrastive limitation).
Even just looking is fun (minimum concession).

prompt.context_jp: 犯人___同じ屋根の下にいる――その考えが二人の肩を重くする。
prompt.prompt_jp: 犯人___同じ屋根の下にいる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 犯人 in this declarative realization.

feedback.correct_en: The 犯人 has already been introduced in the discourse; now the narrator comments ABOUT the culprit. は marks the established topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would re-introduce 犯人 as new information, which doesn't match — we already know a culprit exists; the point is WHERE they are.

contrast_examples.en: The culprit is nearby (known topic — は).
Ah, there's the culprit! (discovery — が)

prompt.context_jp: 「絶対に 犯人___映ってるはずなんです！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 絶対に 犯人___映ってるはずなんです！
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle Mai uses to assert the culprit must be in the footage.

feedback.correct_en: Mai is asserting the EXISTENCE of the culprit on the footage — a yet-unidentified subject. が introduces this emphatic claim of presence.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presume 犯人 is already a known topic being commented on, weakening the discovery/assertion force Mai intends.

contrast_examples.en: The culprit is on camera! (identification — が)
The culprit was caught (topic update — は).

prompt.context_jp: 「分からないんですよ 顔___映ってないんですから」
prompt.prompt_jp: 顔___映ってないんですから。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 顔 when explaining why they can't identify the person.

feedback.correct_en: In a subordinate ので/から clause describing a concrete situation ('because the face isn't shown'), が naturally marks the subject of the state.
feedback.incorrect_en: 顔は would set up a contrast ('as for the face... — but something else is shown'), which isn't the intent here — Mai simply explains the fact.

contrast_examples.en: The face can't be seen (plain situation — が).

contrast_examples.jp: 顔は見えないが、声は聞こえる。
contrast_examples.en: The face can't be seen, but the voice can (contrast — は/は).

prompt.context_jp: 「伊丹グループの給与データを 盗み出したの___あなたですよね？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 盗み出したの___あなたですよね？
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle in this cleft identification.

feedback.correct_en: In the 〜のは〜だ cleft construction, the backgrounded presupposition ('the one who stole it') is marked with は, and the identified answer (あなた) follows.
feedback.incorrect_en: のが would make the clause the subject of a new predicate, not a cleft 'the X is Y' structure. を doesn't fit — 〜の is nominal.

contrast_examples.en: The one who did it is him (cleft — のは).
HE did it (plain identification — が).

prompt.context_jp: 「なんで それ___俺だって 分かるんだよ？」
prompt.prompt_jp: なんで それ___俺だって 分かるんだよ？
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle Seiichiro uses challenging the identification.

feedback.correct_en: In the embedded clause 'that THAT is me,' それ is the subject of a judgment being questioned — exhaustive identification needs が.
feedback.incorrect_en: それは would topicalize それ for broader commentary, losing the pointed 'how do you know THAT (specifically) is me' force.

contrast_examples.en: This is me (identification — が).
This isn't me (comment — は).

prompt.context_jp: 「データだって返したんだし」
prompt.prompt_jp: データ___返したんだし。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits Seiichiro's deflective tone ('I even returned the data...').

feedback.correct_en: データだって carries the dismissive 'even the data (at least) I returned' nuance — a concessive contrast implying 'so what's the big deal.'
feedback.incorrect_en: データは would merely topicalize without the 'even' concession. データが would spotlight the data as new information, which doesn't fit the whiny tone.

contrast_examples.jp: 謝りだってしたんだから。
contrast_examples.en: I even apologized, you know (concessive — だって).

contrast_examples.jp: 謝りはしたが、心からではない。
contrast_examples.en: I did apologize, but not sincerely (contrast — は).

prompt.context_jp: 一歩前へ進み出たの___相馬だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 一歩前へ進み出たの___相馬だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle in this cleft sentence.

feedback.correct_en: 〜のは〜だった is a cleft: 'The one who stepped forward was Souma.' The backgrounded relative clause is marked with は.
feedback.incorrect_en: のが would make the whole clause the subject of a different predicate, not an identificational cleft.

contrast_examples.jp: 立ち上がったのは彼だ。
contrast_examples.en: The one who stood up was him (cleft).
He stood up (plain subject — が).

prompt.context_jp: 「そもそも 君に___ ここで働く資格なんかない」
prompt.prompt_jp: 君に___ ここで働く資格なんかない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 君に in Souma's rebuke.

feedback.correct_en: には carries contrastive emphasis: 'YOU (unlike others who do deserve to work here) don't have the right.' The は after に delivers the pointed contrast.
feedback.incorrect_en: にが is ungrammatical. にも ('also for you') would flip the meaning to inclusion, which contradicts Souma's exclusion.

contrast_examples.en: For YOU, it's impossible (contrast — には).
Even you should understand (inclusion — にも).

prompt.context_jp: 「私___花咲君を呼びました」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私___花咲君を呼びました。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose Karashima's particle when revealing he was the one who recruited Mai.

feedback.correct_en: Karashima is answering the implicit question 'who recruited her?' with himself as the exhaustive answer. が highlights 私 as the specific agent.
feedback.incorrect_en: 私は would make it a general comment about himself, losing the 'it was I (not anyone else)' revelation force.

contrast_examples.en: I was the one who did it (identification — が).
As for me, I oppose (topic — は).

prompt.context_jp: 「花咲 お前___間違ってない」
prompt.prompt_jp: お前___間違ってない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle in Souma's gentle affirmation.

feedback.correct_en: Souma addresses Mai directly, commenting about her: 'YOU (the one standing here) are not wrong.' は marks her as the topic of judgment.
feedback.incorrect_en: お前が間違ってない would awkwardly imply exhaustive listing ('it's YOU who is not wrong'), which isn't the warm supportive tone intended.

contrast_examples.en: You are right (judgment about you — は).
YOU (not them) are the right one (exhaustive — が).

prompt.context_jp: 「この銀行で働く人たち___ いちばん大事であってほしいです」
prompt.prompt_jp: この銀行で働く人たち___ いちばん大事であってほしいです。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose Mai's particle emphasizing WHO should matter most.

feedback.correct_en: Mai answers 'what is important?' by picking out this group as the exhaustive answer against Shindo's 'profit.' が identifies them as the ones who should matter most.
feedback.incorrect_en: 人たちは would weaken this to a general topic comment, losing the pointed contrast with Shindo's answer.

contrast_examples.en: People are what matter (identificational — が).
People, yes, are important (general topic — は).

prompt.context_jp: 「7階の男子トイレ___ 置いてあったそうだ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 7階の男子トイレ___ 置いてあったそうだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the location where the data was left.

feedback.correct_en: With 置いてある (resultative state of being placed), the location of existence is marked with に, not the action location で.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark where an action occurs, but 置いてある focuses on the resulting state — the data existing AT that spot.

contrast_examples.jp: 机にメモが置いてある。
contrast_examples.en: A memo is placed on the desk (existence — に).
I write a letter at the desk (action — で).

prompt.context_jp: 「ハァ… それは ___の幸いだった」
prompt.prompt_jp: それは ___の幸いだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the set-phrase expression.

feedback.correct_en: 不幸中の幸い is the fixed idiom meaning 'a silver lining / fortunate within misfortune.' Shindo uses it on hearing the data wasn't accessed.
feedback.incorrect_en: The other combinations aren't established idioms in Japanese; only 不幸中の幸い is a conventional set phrase.

contrast_examples.jp: 怪我が軽くて不幸中の幸いだった。
contrast_examples.en: The injury was light — a silver lining in misfortune.
That was lucky (not an idiom).

prompt.context_jp: 「はい 行きましょう 相馬さん “___は急げ”です」
prompt.prompt_jp: “___は急げ”です。
prompt.prompt_en: Complete the proverb Mai cites.

feedback.correct_en: 善は急げ ('do good deeds quickly / strike while the iron is hot') is the standard proverb — Mai urges Souma to act immediately.
feedback.incorrect_en: 急は急げ / 時は急げ aren't established proverbs. The fixed form is 善は急げ.

contrast_examples.jp: 善は急げと言うから、今やろう。
contrast_examples.en: They say 'strike while the iron is hot,' so let's do it now.
Haste makes waste (opposite proverb).

prompt.context_jp: 「ここから手がかりを見つけだすのは ___が折れるぞ」
prompt.prompt_jp: ここから手がかりを見つけだすのは ___が折れるぞ。
prompt.prompt_en: Complete the idiom meaning 'strenuous / arduous work.'

feedback.correct_en: 骨が折れる is the fixed idiom meaning 'to be arduous / require great effort.' Souma uses it about the tedious footage review.
feedback.incorrect_en: 腕が折れる literally means 'break an arm.' 気が折れる is not a standard idiom (気が滅入る/折れる心 exist but not 気が折れる in this sense).

contrast_examples.jp: この仕事は骨が折れる。
contrast_examples.en: This job is arduous.
A skilled craftsman (different idiom — 腕が立つ).

prompt.context_jp: 「___をくくったら どうですか？ もう言い逃れできませんよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: ___をくくったら どうですか？
prompt.prompt_en: Complete Souma's idiom telling Seiichiro to resign himself to the truth.

feedback.correct_en: 腹をくくる means 'to steel oneself / brace for the inevitable.' Souma presses Seiichiro to accept the facts and stop making excuses.
feedback.incorrect_en: 首をくくる means to hang oneself — a very different, grim idiom. 頭をくくる is not a standard expression.

contrast_examples.jp: 腹をくくって、本当のことを話した。
contrast_examples.en: I steeled myself and told the truth.
To make up one's mind (near synonym).

prompt.context_jp: 「どうなることかと 思っていたが ___転じて 福となったんじゃないか？」
prompt.prompt_jp: ___転じて 福となったんじゃないか？
prompt.prompt_en: Complete the four-character idiom (災い転じて福となす).

feedback.correct_en: 災い転じて福となす means 'turning misfortune into fortune' — the fixed form uses 災い, not alternative synonyms.
feedback.incorrect_en: The idiom is lexically fixed; swapping 不運 or 失敗 breaks the proverb even though they share meaning.

contrast_examples.en: Turn misfortune into fortune (fixed proverb).
Failure is the mother of success (different proverb).

prompt.context_jp: 「___を返すようですが… 全ての人たちではありません」
prompt.prompt_jp: ___を返すようですが…
prompt.prompt_en: Complete the polite set phrase prefacing respectful disagreement.

feedback.correct_en: お言葉を返すようですが is the fixed polite preface meaning 'I'm sorry to contradict you, but...' used before pushing back on a superior.
feedback.incorrect_en: ご意見を返す / お話を返す aren't the conventional set phrase. The idiom is fixed with お言葉.

contrast_examples.jp: お言葉を返すようですが、そうは思いません。
contrast_examples.en: I'm sorry to contradict you, but I don't think so.

contrast_examples.jp: 失礼ですが、違うと思います。
contrast_examples.en: Excuse me, but I think it's different (less formal pushback).

prompt.context_jp: 「“言うこと聞かないと どうなるか分かってるのか”って 伊丹さんに___れて…」
prompt.prompt_jp: 伊丹さんに___れて…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the passive verb Kameda uses to describe Itami's threat.

feedback.correct_en: 脅される ('to be threatened') fits the quoted intimidation ('you know what'll happen if you don't obey'). Kameda is explaining he acted under threat.
feedback.incorrect_en: 叱られる means 'to be scolded' — too mild for the menacing quote. 頼まれる ('to be asked') contradicts the coercive wording.

contrast_examples.jp: 脅されて仕方なく従った。
contrast_examples.en: I was threatened and had no choice but to comply.
I was asked and helped (voluntary).

prompt.context_jp: 「あんた 間違いなく___れるぞ」
prompt.prompt_jp: あんた 間違いなく___れるぞ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb Seiichiro uses meaning 'get banished / transferred to a dead-end post.'

feedback.correct_en: 飛ばされる in corporate-slang usage means 'to be shipped off to a bad assignment' — the exact threat Seiichiro makes about Mai being punished.
feedback.incorrect_en: 送られる is neutral 'be sent' without the punitive nuance. 切られる means 'be fired/cut,' but transfer not termination is implied.

contrast_examples.en: He was shipped off to the sticks (demotion nuance).
He was sent to the regions (neutral).

prompt.context_jp: 坂田が伊丹清一郎に調査中であることを謝罪するとき
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds most natural as a formal business apology for an ongoing investigation?

choices.text: 申し訳ございません。ただいま調査中ですので…
ごめんなさい。今調べていますので…
すまない。調査しているから…

feedback.correct_en: 申し訳ございません + ただいま調査中 matches the formal business register required when addressing an angry client representative.
feedback.incorrect_en: ごめんなさい is too casual for business apology. すまない is informal/male-casual, inappropriate to a client.

contrast_examples.jp: 申し訳ございません。確認いたします。
contrast_examples.en: We apologize. We'll verify (business-formal).
Sorry, I'm checking (casual among friends).

prompt.context_jp: 真藤本部長が深く頭を下げる伊丹会長に声をかけるとき
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing is most natural when politely asking a bowing elder to raise his head?

choices.text: 伊丹さん、頭をお上げください。
伊丹さん、頭を上げてね。

feedback.correct_en: お+Verb-stem+ください is the standard respectful request form appropriate when addressing an elder of status like Chairman Itami.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜てね is casual/intimate — unsuitable for a client chairman. 上げろ is a blunt command, extremely rude in this context.

contrast_examples.jp: どうぞお座りください。
contrast_examples.en: Please have a seat (respectful request).
Have a seat, OK? (casual).

prompt.context_jp: 仕事終わりの打ち上げの食事会で
prompt.prompt_en: Which pair sounds most natural to open a work-done celebratory toast?

choices.text: お疲れさまでした！ 乾杯！
ご苦労さまでした！ 乾杯！

feedback.correct_en: お疲れさまでした is the standard peer/mixed-rank acknowledgment of work; combined with 乾杯 it's the natural toast opener.
feedback.incorrect_en: ご苦労さま is used downward (superior → subordinate) and sounds presumptuous here. 疲れた！飲もう！ is too crude for a mixed group with bosses present.

contrast_examples.jp: お疲れさまです、乾杯しましょう。
contrast_examples.en: Good work everyone, let's toast.
Good job (said down to subordinates).

prompt.context_jp: 坂田が出向を受け入れて舞に語るとき
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds most natural as Sakata's resigned explanation of corporate reality?

choices.text: 何かあったら誰かが責任を取る、それが銀行だからな。
何かがあると誰かは責任を取るので、それは銀行です。
何かあったら誰かに責任を取らせる、それこそ銀行だ。

feedback.correct_en: The original rhythm — conditional 〜たら, generic 誰か, final 〜だからな — carries natural resigned-wisdom tone a senior would use with a junior.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option b misuses が/は and the explanatory ので/です sequence sounds stilted and textbook-like. Option c shifts to causative 取らせる and the emphatic それこそ, changing the meaning to blame-shifting rather than resigned acceptance.

contrast_examples.jp: それが会社ってもんだ。
contrast_examples.en: That's just how companies are (natural resigned tone).

contrast_examples.jp: それは会社というものです。
contrast_examples.en: That is a thing called a company (stilted, textbook).

prompt.context_jp: 舞がアジフライに醤油をかける派だと主張するとき
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds most natural for Mai's casual food-preference argument?

choices.text: 醤油でさっぱりいただくのがいいんですよ！
醤油でさっぱりに食べるのが良いのです！
醤油をさっぱりといただくのがいいんですよ！

feedback.correct_en: さっぱりいただく (adverbial さっぱり modifying いただく) is the natural collocation. で marks soy sauce as the means. The 〜のがいいんですよ frame fits her lively peer-register argument.
feedback.incorrect_en: さっぱりに is ungrammatical — さっぱり is already adverbial without に. 醤油を…いただく makes soy sauce the direct object, which doesn't fit the 'with soy sauce' meaning.

contrast_examples.jp: レモンでさっぱりいただく。
contrast_examples.en: Enjoy it refreshingly with lemon (natural).

contrast_examples.jp: レモンをさっぱりいただく。
contrast_examples.en: *Eat the lemon refreshingly (odd meaning).
